continuity.history: .execution/box-v4/ is frozen history for B0-B1.1, D1.1 and D1.2. New work is recorded in waves/<id>.md, STATUS.md and Git.
continuity.sequence: Product: D4 waits for the owner. Kitchen: K4 (numbers and stall guard) -> K5 (no repeat work) -> K6 (template database) -> K7 (typecheck and workers), each measured before and after.

sharedIntegrationPolicy: Each wave brief names its write paths. One writer per branch; the reviewer checks the diff stays inside them. Globs below are planning scope.
evidenceDirectoryPattern: waves/<taskId>.md holds the brief and the reviewer result; verify logs are local under .kitchen/runs/.

tasks.title: Select the supported delegation case and reconcile reusable foundations
deliverables: Record actual W002 acceptance/ownership and the exact reusable Box, auth, Git, environment and evaluation interfaces; distinguish checked source from accepted behavior.

Specify one modular TypeScript fixture repository and two bounded work requests, including a shared dependency, unrelated excluded owner modules, literal completion examples and an unsupported coupling case.

Define the initial buyer/job, documented competitive overlap and an ordinary issue-plus-contributor comparison before final results. Predeclare comparable obligations, input/tool/familiarity differences, observations and classification; do not start a customer study or procure vendor access.
Prepare the first implementation brief with exact integration paths and resource/recipient policy; retain B history and the current implementation candidate.
acceptance: A reviewer can identify the first supported task, required package inputs, owner integration obligations and why no full owner clone should be necessary.

The comparison protocol accounts for common onboarding, per-task preparation, recipient setup, owner verification/integration and rework; missing observations and commercial evidence remain unverified.
No current lease is taken or old task accepted by inference. Dependent implementation awaits independently accepted B1.1 or an explicit separately approved replacement foundation.
verification: Independent source/interface and fixture-design review; read-only reconciliation, no product test or new resource is required for this planning unit.

tasks.title: Verify on the host without Docker
deliverables: Refresh the lockfile so packages/box-contracts is installed by a normal frozen install; today test:box-contracts cannot resolve zod on the host.
Add an embedded Postgres provider to scripts/verify.mjs and make it the default, so verification needs no Docker.
Box test helpers accept the disposable database verify provides: no fixed container hostname, no database cap, each run creates and drops its own databases.
Remove the W002 verification profile switches from scripts/suite.mjs and scripts/vitest.config.mjs once nothing uses them. Leave scripts/box-verification in place, unused, until a later cleanup.
acceptance: With Docker Desktop stopped, node scripts/verify.mjs test:box-contracts test:box-auth exits 0 on a clean clone after a frozen install.
A second run immediately afterwards also passes and leaves no databases, processes or containers behind.
No assertion in an existing Box test is weakened.
verification: Reviewer repeats both runs with Docker stopped and compares the Box test assertions with master.

tasks.title: Prepare a versioned Box from a work request and completion agreement
reuse: B2.1/B2.2/B4 design seams, not their unverified completion
deliverables: Instantiate the D1.1 fixture design with a pinned isolated owner Git baseline and reproducible fixture registration; shared helpers and excluded modules must be actual source, not prose placeholders.
Direct request or pasted issue body plus registered repository/base produces a draft with grounded facts, observable examples, exclusions and unresolved preparation gaps.
Owner can understand and approve the exact completion agreement through a concise card or input/output example; no mandatory chat, external tracker connector or handwritten technical spec.
Changed agreement creates a new version and invalidates affected approval; intake remains separate from assignment, execution and bounty publication.
acceptance: Both supported requests produce inspectable drafts through the same preparation path. A recorded URL is not claimed as fetched content.
Unresolved consequential requirements and stale approval block readiness. Demo output, live-model evidence and independently assessed requirement quality are distinct.
A request may contain connected full-stack work; the system does not equate each sentence with a separate Box.
verification: Real owner UI/API create, approve and amend flow; independent literal agreement/version/role tests and an omitted-obligation negative case.
tasks.resumption: Held by the CEO on 5 October 2026 as unaccepted work on branch wave/D1.2. Resume after K1: rebase onto master, move its tests to the disposable database, drop its container harness, then review and verify under KITCHEN.md.

tasks.title: Export and validate the actual portable work package
reuse: packages/analyzer import scanning where it fits
deliverables: A Box is a plain folder: box.json (outcome, base commit, read context, editable paths, checks, submission contract), the selected source, the lockfile and tool versions, and non-sensitive fixtures. No server, database or container is required to create or open one.

A command-line export builds that folder from an owner-reviewed manifest and reports every import that leaves the selection, so a missing dependency is a named preparation gap rather than a silent full-repository fallback.
Export validates itself by execution: install and run the declared baseline checks in a clean directory that contains only the package. Excluded modules may be replaced by declared type-only stubs.
Record package inventory, the share of owner source disclosed, transfer sizes and actual preparation effort and corrections.
The agreement can come from a file. The D1.2 store is one source of agreements, not a prerequisite.
acceptance: In a clean directory with no owner repository or history, the package installs, builds its baseline and runs its declared checks using only Node, pnpm and Git.
An omitted dependency, an escaping path or link, an unlisted input and an attempt to reach owner-only source are each rejected with a reason.
Unrelated owner modules are demonstrably absent from the package. Exporting the full owner source cannot pass this gate.
verification: Reviewer runs export and the clean-directory checks on the supported fixture and on one slice of this repository, plus the missing-dependency and boundary negatives.
tasks.approach: Start with a prototype wave: two or three small throwaway attempts at selecting source for one fixture change (for example an owner-written manifest checked by import closure, selection derived from the TypeScript program starting at the editable paths, and type-only stubs for everything outside the editable paths). Compare them on the same clean-directory checks, disclosed-source share and preparation effort, then write the real brief from the winner.

tasks.title: Open the package and submit an exact scoped contribution
reuse: Box attempt identity fields from packages/box-contracts
deliverables: A recipient opens the folder in any editor or hands it to any agent, implements inside the editable paths and runs the local checks.
A command-line submit produces a patch bound to the Box identity, version and base commit, with paths mapped back to owner source.
Record who or what the recipient was, what it was given, setup and investigation effort, and every clarification it needed. For agent recipients also record tokens and whether it succeeded.
The first real recipients are this kitchen's own workers: a wave brief is delivered as a Box.
acceptance: An actual recipient completes open, edit, local check and submit using the package only. A simulated recipient does not count.
Edits outside the editable paths, a wrong Box or base, and an altered agreement are rejected at submit and again at owner verification.
Human and agent recipients use the same package and the same checks.
verification: Reviewer performs a real package-only attempt and the wrong-scope, wrong-version and altered-agreement cases.

tasks.title: Verify the contribution in the original repository and integrate it
reuse: packages/evaluation patch validation where it fits
deliverables: A command-line verify applies the exact submitted patch to a clean checkout of the owner repository at the Box base and runs the owner-side checks, including the surrounding interfaces the package did not contain.
A stale base or failed check blocks integration. On pass, the owner merges through ordinary Git with the Box and attempt identity in the commit message.
Each failure is classified: preparation defect (the package lacked something), environment failure, or implementation failure against a published obligation.
acceptance: A correct supported contribution integrates into real owner Git history with recoverable Box/attempt/review provenance.
Local-pass/full-owner-fail, self-review, stale result and absent merge authority cannot become accepted.
No production release, remote publication or payment is inferred from accepted synthetic integration.
verification: Reviewer runs a real patch through verify and merge on the fixture, plus stale-base, repeat-submission and local-pass-owner-fail negatives.

tasks.title: Expose the minimal prepare, delegate and accept journey on the web
reuse: B4 list/detail and B6 truthful history designs
Existing auth, assignment and safe UI projections
deliverables: A requester prepares/approves a request, sees package readiness and assigns one trusted recipient; recipient opens/submits; owner sees independent evidence and permitted acceptance/integration action.
Show concise outcome, actual owner, status, preparation gaps and next action. Detail remains accessible; no raw hashes or dependency editing required for ordinary use.
Use existing web shell and adapters; avoid mandatory conversation, rich universal previews, marketplace or a general team scheduler.

Owner selects an authorised trusted contributor/adapter through existing identities and permissions; no provider-supplied workforce is required. Record owner review/integration effort without adding a metrics form to normal use.
acceptance: A complete supported Box is navigable through the common API with honest proposed, ready, in-progress, review and accepted states.
Reload/resume preserves server authority, versions and evidence; unsupported/failed work is visible and never displayed as completed.
The simple UI does not conceal material scope/approval decisions or grant executor acceptance rights.
verification: Independent browser/API walkthrough, role and stale-state cases, keyboard-readable actions and truthful preparation/acceptance gaps.
tasks.deferred: After the D4 decision. Build it only if D4 recommends continuing, and shape it around what D4 showed users actually needed.

tasks.title: Demonstrate independent package-only delegation and counterexamples
deliverables: Run the two supported changes with a fresh approved recipient context using only the exported package; retain supplied-input and command evidence plus owner integration results.
Exercise missing dependency/obligation, unsupported coupling, local-pass/full-owner-fail, stale version and out-of-scope submission cases.
State whether the recipient already knew the fixture, which dependencies were cached, and which AI/human claims remain untested.

Run the predeclared ordinary delegation comparison when the approved wave authorises its runtime/inputs/resources; retain equivalent outcomes and acceptance, disclose access/learning differences and include failed attempts. Missing authority or comparability is an evidence gap, never an invented baseline.

Compare each agent recipient given the Box with the same agent given the full repository: success, tokens, elapsed time and owner interventions. Report the share of owner source disclosed for every Box.
acceptance: At least two actual package-only contributions complete the full approved loop; full owner source cannot be supplied to manufacture portability.
At least one unsupported package fails readiness honestly and every required negative case retains its correct non-pass classification.
A separate-context agent is not called a recruited human or hostile isolation proof. Real participants/external messaging/payments need separate authorised pilots.
verification: Reviewer audits inputs and artifacts end to end on the current commit and reruns at least one delegation from a clean directory.

tasks.title: Assess delegation effort, repeat-use evidence and the next product decision
deliverables: Report owner preparation, recipient setup/investigation, clarification, omissions, source/dependency transfer, verification, integration and rework across successes and failures.
Compare with an explicitly documented ordinary delegation baseline where actual comparable data exists; absent baseline or paid/customer evidence remains unverified.

Report software capability, measured effort, actual repeat use and commercial commitment/payment as separate conclusions. Prepare a customer-pilot protocol and blank recording instruments for the initial buyer; no outreach, customer/private-data access or payments occur without a separately approved pilot.

Recommend extend supported classes, simplify preparation, conduct an authorised customer pilot, or stop/reframe. Bounties/payments, restricted disclosure and broad PM previews remain separate proposals.
acceptance: Results distinguish portable software capability from utility, demand, novelty, confidentiality and universal task breadth.

Reported effort includes common onboarding, preparation, recipient work, verification/integration and failures at comparable quality. Interview interest cannot count as repeat use, a pricing answer as payment or synthetic success as customer adoption; absent pilot evidence stays unverified without fabricating a result.
D4 closure supplies one short evidence-backed CEO decision and reproducible known-supported runbook; it never starts the next stage automatically.
verification: Independent metric/artifact reconciliation, all-attempt denominator and reproducible fresh-start instructions; empty customer-study data remains explicitly empty.

tasks.title: Move the legacy live tests onto the disposable database
deliverables: The tests named *-live.test.ts that only need a database run against the Postgres that scripts/verify.mjs provides, instead of shelling into the private-task-mvp-synthetic containers.
Tests that genuinely need the running legacy services are listed with the reason and moved out of check into their own package script, unchanged.
check passes twice in a row with no wait, because nothing in it hits the legacy login rate limiter any more.
acceptance: node scripts/verify.mjs exits 0 twice back to back.
No assertion in any moved test is weakened; each still fails when the behaviour it guards is broken.
With the four private-task-mvp-synthetic containers stopped, check still passes.
verification: Reviewer stops the synthetic containers, runs verify twice, restarts them, and compares each ported assertion with master.

tasks.title: Remove the old container verification harness
deliverables: scripts/box-verification/, tests/box/verification/ and the mailbox transport in scripts/docker.mjs are deleted, with the BOX_VERIFICATION_* switches in scripts/suite.mjs and scripts/vitest.config.mjs.
tests/box/auth/fixture-transport.test.ts goes with the transport it tested. This removal of tests is the stated purpose of the wave and is named in its brief.
acceptance: No file references BOX_VERIFICATION_ or scripts/box-verification.
node scripts/verify.mjs test:box-contracts test:box-auth test:box-delegation exits 0.
verification: Reviewer greps for leftovers and confirms no test outside the old harness was removed or changed.

tasks.title: Kitchen numbers page and a stall guard in verify
deliverables: node scripts/kitchen-stats.mjs prints one page from .kitchen/runs and Git: verify minutes per step, runs and failed runs per wave branch, wave duration from first commit to merge, and the three largest costs. No new files to maintain; it only reads.

scripts/verify.mjs counts consecutive non-PASS runs and elapsed time on the current branch from its own run history, and prints a plain STALL line telling the agent to park the wave once a threshold is passed (defaults: 6 consecutive non-PASS committed runs or 90 minutes; thresholds are flags). It never changes the verdict or exit code.
acceptance: On the 5 October night-run logs the page reproduces the known figures: about 120 verify minutes, check about 45.
A test feeds verify a fabricated run history and sees the STALL line appear at the threshold and not before.
PASS, FAIL and UNCOMMITTED verdicts and exit codes are unchanged.
verification: Reviewer recomputes two figures by hand from the summaries and runs the stall test with thresholds on both sides.

tasks.title: Verify speed 1: stop repeating work
deliverables: A step that already passed on this exact commit, with a clean tree, is not run again: verify reads its own summaries, reports the step as reused with the run it came from, and --fresh forces a real run. A reused result is never offered for a dirty tree or a different commit.
A suite named in the brief is not run a second time inside the same invocation when check already ran it.

check runs the typecheck, the boundary check and only the suites whose paths the branch touched since master; a change to shared tooling (scripts/, package.json, the lockfile, test config) runs everything. --full runs every suite, and the head chef runs --full before a milestone closes and before each overnight stop.

KITCHEN.md and the reviewer role say what this means for the pass: it may rely on a recorded PASS for the same commit and spend its time on the diff, the lenses and its own attacks; it runs --fresh when it has any reason to doubt the record.
acceptance: Before and after come from scripts/kitchen-stats.mjs (K4), at least five runs each on the same commit, with spread. Keep a change only if the numbers support it.
A deliberately broken test in a suite the branch did not touch is still caught by --full.
Changing one byte and committing invalidates every reused result for that branch.
No assertion is removed or weakened.
verification: Reviewer re-measures on its own runs, breaks one test in an untouched suite to confirm --full catches it, and tries to obtain a reused PASS for a commit that never passed.
tasks.baseline: Night run of 5 October 2026: 120 verify minutes in 398; 11 of 25 passing runs repeated suites that had already passed on the same commit (37 minutes); check about 106 s per run; the auth suite ran 18 times.
lenses: security: the reuse record is the thing being trusted; try to get a false PASS out of it

tasks.title: Verify speed 2: clone a migrated template database
deliverables: verify migrates one template database per run for each migration set, and test helpers create their database with CREATE DATABASE ... TEMPLATE instead of replaying every migration per test file.
The template is rebuilt whenever the migration files change (key it on their content), has no open connections when it is cloned, and is dropped with the run.
One test still migrates from empty, so a broken migration cannot hide behind a stale template.
acceptance: Before and after come from scripts/kitchen-stats.mjs (K4), at least five runs each on the same commit, with spread. Keep a change only if the numbers support it.
A migration edited after the template was built is reflected in the next run.
Nothing is left behind after verify.
verification: Reviewer adds a throwaway migration, confirms the next run sees it, removes it, and re-measures.

tasks.title: Verify speed 3: typecheck and parallel workers
deliverables: Try, smallest first, and keep only what the numbers support: incremental typecheck with its cache under .kitchen/; two or three test workers instead of one, each with its own database, within the 16 GB limit; the native TypeScript 7 compiler for the typecheck step only.

packages/analyzer uses the TypeScript 6 compiler API. If TypeScript 7 is adopted for typechecking, the analyzer keeps the version it needs and both are pinned; if that cannot be done cleanly, record why and stop.
Any test that only passed because it ran alone is fixed or reported by name, not hidden by going back to one worker without saying so.
acceptance: Before and after come from scripts/kitchen-stats.mjs (K4), at least five runs each on the same commit, with spread. Keep a change only if the numbers support it.
Typecheck results are identical before and after on a commit with a deliberate type error.
Peak memory during verify is recorded and stays within what the machine can give.
verification: Reviewer introduces a type error and an order-dependent test on a scratch branch and confirms both are caught.
